cards.front: Recall a key point about The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC)
cards.back: The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC) was a rebellion of Greek city-states in Asia Minor against Persian rule

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC)
cards.back: Aristagoras, tyrant of Miletus, initiated the revolt after a failed attack on Naxos left him fearing Persian punishment

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC)
cards.back: Athens sent 20 ships and Eretria sent 5 to support the Ionians — this enraged King Darius

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC)
cards.back: The burning of Sardis (498 BC) was the revolt's greatest success but provoked a devastating Persian response

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC)
cards.back: The revolt was crushed at the Battle of Lade (494 BC); Miletus was sacked and its people enslaved

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC)
cards.back: Herodotus is our main source; he presents the revolt as the beginning of the chain of events leading to the Persian Wars
